default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1208.title: Thin-volume shock bar fade
E-1208.hypothesis: A bar with an outsized body on below-normal volume for the minute was pushed by few participants; liquidity providers who took the other side see it revert.

E-1209.title: Held bar gap follow
E-1209.hypothesis: A bar opening beyond the previous bar's extreme and closing still beyond it shows resting orders overwhelmed at the open of the bar; the imbalance continues.

E-1210.title: Prior-day bias day-open cross
E-1210.hypothesis: After an up (down) previous session, returning above (below) the day's open after a spell on the other side signals that the prior day's holders are back in control.

E-1211.title: Volatility squeeze release
E-1211.hypothesis: When the recent window range is small versus typical for 20 sessions, resting stops pile up on both sides; the first close beyond the window releases them in that direction.

E-1212.title: Balance-day extreme fade
E-1212.hypothesis: On a session whose range after 11:00 is still small against the previous day's, a new session extreme attracts breakout buyers into a two-sided market; fade the poke.

E-1213.title: VWAP slope flip
E-1213.hypothesis: When the session VWAP turns direction and price sits on that side, the average cost of the day's volume is moving with price; follow the first bar of agreement.

E-1214.title: Rolling VWAP vs session VWAP cross
E-1214.hypothesis: Recent volume-weighted price crossing the whole-session VWAP shows that recent flow is paid at a different level than the day's average; follow the change.

E-1215.title: One-sided close count exhaustion
E-1215.hypothesis: When nearly every recent close is higher (lower) than the one before, the move is crowded and late buyers (sellers) have no one left to recruit; fade it.

E-1217.title: US-open impulse follow
E-1217.hypothesis: At the New York cash open (10:30 or 11:30 Brasilia time) foreign flow enters; the first minutes' direction in the index future is followed by the rest of the participants.

E-1216.title: PTAX window move fade
E-1216.hypothesis: Dollar flow tied to the PTAX fixing windows (10, 11, 12, 13h) is mechanical, not informational; a large move inside the window tends to revert once the window closes.
